newsitem.title: PERU: Maoist rebels bomb Peru power firm, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Maoist rebels bomb Peru power firm, no injuries.

text.p: Suspected Maoist rebels tossed a bomb at an electric company early on Sunday on the outskirts of the Peruvian capital of Lima, shattering windows and causing minor damage, police said.
"There were no injuries and no deaths," Lieutenent Franco Ruiz of the Peruvian police bomb squad UDEX told Reuters.
Police said Shining Path guerrillas drove by in a car and threw a package containing 300 to 400 grams of dynamite at electrical generator Edelnor and tossed out leaflets before fleeing from the site.
The blast shattered windows for a block around and caused damage at a nearby hostel, he added.
The company is located in Canto Grande, a poor district in eastern greater Lima.
Peru's two rebel groups, the Shining Path and smaller Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), have often bombed government and business installations in 16 years of guerrilla wars.
A group of 15 heavily armed MRTA guerrillas are currently holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima. The hostage crisis is in its 54th day.
The Shining Path, which remains a stronger group, has kept a low profile and has been largely overshadowed by the MRTA since the Dec. 17 storming of a cocktail party at the ambassador's home.
Guerrilla wars in Peru have killed 30,000 people and caused $25 billlion in damage since the Shining Path first took up arms against the Peruvian state in 1980.
